newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses climb, ignoring unsteady Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses climb, ignoring unsteady Wall St.

text.p: European bourses climbed sharply on Tuesday, with some hitting new peaks, despite an unsteady opening on Wall Street after a record-breaking run.
On currency markets, the dollar recovered from two-month lows against the mark on supportive remarks by Bundesbank council members.
Frankfurt and Amsterdam stocks broke records and Paris shares surged to a new high for the year as the stronger dollar was seen as offering improved potental for European exporters.

European investors went on a buying spree, shrugging off Tuesday's losses on Wall Street which saw its fourth consecutive record close on Monday. Wall Street recovered some of the losses in later trade.
Frankfurt surged to a record intra-day high on the IBIS DAX index in computerised transactions as the dollar strengthened.

The 30-share IBIS DAX jumped to an all-time trading peak of 2,765.61 points before slipping back slightly towards the close. The previous best was set only last Friday. Floor trading ended up slightly.
In Amsterdam, Dutch shares ended at a fresh closing high, the second in two days after coming close to breaking through the 600 level on AEX share index for the first time.
The index closed 0.49 points higher at 597.59. It reached to 599.69 in the opening hours of the session, buoyed by another record high closing overnight on Wall Street.
French stocks recovered their composure after slipping in early trade to end at 2229.13 points, a gain of 1.09 percent and the highest close of the year.

Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister said the current dollar exchange rate was "not appropriate". The dollar rose, which heartened French investors as dollar strength could help U.S. appetite for foreign assets.

In London, stocks built up a head of steam in early trading drawing strength from Wall Street's fourth consecutive record close on Monday. The momentum kept London ahead, even when Wall Street opened in the minus column on Tuesday.
But traders and strategists say further gains are likely to be limited until the British budget is released on November 26.

"Cash levels are very high at the moment, but I don't think anyone is going to be comfortable putting it into the market this side of the budget," said Tim Russell, head of UK equities at Lazard Investors.

Meister's comments, coupled with remarks by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp that he believed a stronger dollar might be more appropriate, helped the dollar recover from lows against the mark.
The U.S. currency edged over the 1.50-mark level in late European trade, propelled by the Bundesbank comments.
Currency analysts said with a full schedule of Bundesbank officials speaking over the next three days, these comments could be the start of a fresh round of verbal dollar support.
"Clearly what we're seeing is the Bundesbank go into a strategy of verbal support for the dollar," said James McKay, international economist at PaineWebber in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5012 marks and 111.47 yen, compared with 1.4983 marks and 111.20 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 19.9 points higher at 3,934.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 23.93 at 2,229.13.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 5.98 at 2,734.30.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1700 GMT
Gold closed at $381.75 an ounce, one dollar up from Monday's close. Silver ended unchanged at $4.87.
